chapter: Porch interview and Jazz Train plans
title: Jazz and the problem of calling everything jazz
summary: Music has always been part of him but too much is called jazz.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: Well, I'm trying -- I'm still trying. You know? Music has always been a part of me, I liked it and I enjoyed it, but the point of jazz, that's so hard to define -- jazz incorporates so much music. A lot of music that is not jazz is sometimes called jazz.
It's one of those slang terms that doesn't mean what it says, huh?
When you cover too damn much, it just isn't right. There are a lot of things that are not jazz that they all jazz.

That's pretty plain. You can't categorize everything you hear in music as being part of jazz. The music of the time was jazz -- what do you want to take it and throw it back there and put it in the jazz category
for? It doesn't make good sense to me. I think that's pretty reasonable. They just cover too much territory with the word 'jazz'.
